messages:
maya: Heads-up — perf regression in canary after kernel-selector change (v2.3.4). Soft-429s up ~2.4x on 8k+ seq tails. Pasting quick profile and sample logs. Thoughts on token-hedging + smoothing?

samir: oof, can you drop numbers + where we saw kernel switch?

maya: short: majority on gtx-pool-2, selector prefers wave-kern when avg seq >512. New heuristic bumped the boundary 384->512. We saw microbatch assembly time increase ~12ms median, p99 +35ms for sequences that mixed kv hits/misses. soft-429s happened during microburst at 11:07 UTC.

maya: profiling snippet:
```
-- timeline --
request_id=abc123
seq_len=1024
kv_hit_ratio=0.42
kernel_selected=wave-kern-v3
batch_assembly_ms=28.6
compute_launch_ms=2.1
kv_read_ms=6.4
latency_ms=180  -> compared to baseline 145
soft_429=true (admit_reject: probabilistic_shed)
```

maya: aggregated metrics we saw: 
- baseline p99 latency: 220ms
- canary p99 latency: 255ms
- soft-429 rate: baseline 0.3% -> canary 0.75%

lena: could be kv-miss scatter causing batch heterogeneity. wave-kern might have worse cold KV tail. do we have traces?

maya: attaching trace ids: abc123, def456, ghi789 (see logs). Also ran a short sim with token_budget=200 and token_hedge=20 and it reduced soft-429s in sim by ~30% but increased avg cost by ~2%.

ryan: what's token-hedge here?

maya: token-hedge = reserve small per-queue token budget for forming short-tail batches so they don't wait and push batch assembly to long windows. idea: when queue sees a request with small remaining tokens (<hedge) it can bypass normal batching timeout up to N tokens.

samir: seems similar to fast-lane idea but per-token. Need to tune hedge size vs unit-cost. Do we have config prototype?

maya: config we tried:
```
queue.batch.timeout_ms=10
queue.batch.token_budget_target=200
queue.batch.token_hedge=20
queue.batch.hedge_policy=allow_if_kv_hit_ratio>0.3
soft_429.mode=probabilistic
soft_429.base_rate=0.02
soft_429.max_rate=0.15
```

lena: the hedge_policy gating by kv_hit_ratio is interesting — prevents hedging for cold-cache heavy flows. Might help.

ryan: ops note: if we bypass timeout often, kernel choice still matters because microbatches will use wave-kern due to seq_len. Could we add deterministic kernel hint for hedged batches? e.g., force small-batch-optimized kernel for batches with high heterogeneity.

maya: yes that's a thought. We can have runtime set kernel_hint=small-batch when batch_size<6 or kv_stddev>0.25.

samir: also need smoothing on the backpressure signal — current prob_shed reacts to p99 changes quickly causing oscillation. Suggest EWMA over 30s on p99 and soft-429 ramp window 120s.

maya: proposed experiment plan:
1) Canary config: token_hedge=15, hedge_policy kv_hit>0.25, kernel_hint for hedged batches = small-batch-v1, EWMA window=30s for p99 signal.
2) Run 6h canary on gtx-pool-2, compare soft-429, p50/p95/p99, cost delta.
3) Run sim workload with mixed kv hits to validate.

ryan: sg. Add alerting: if soft-429 rate >1% for >5m rollback. :+1:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy at 2026-03-19T02:00Z -> rollout/eng-runtime/canary-3501234567

samir: small nit: also add tracing tag kernel_hint so we can filter in observability.

maya: agree. I'll open a PR with configs + test sim + perf dashboard. Assigning to @samir for telemetry and @ryan for deployment guardrails. Quick volunteers for review?

lena: I'll review telemetry.

samir: i can do dashboard queries.

ryan: I'll review rollback automation.

maya: thanks. TL;DR: probable kernel-selector boundary tweak + kv heterogeneity increased batch assembly variance -> more soft-429s. Short-term mitigation: token-hedge + kernel_hint + signal smoothing. Experiment scheduled. :railway_track:
